verses.text: The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid or lose heart. Take the whole army with you and go up to Ai. Look, I have given you the king of Ai, his people, his city and his land.
Do to Ai and its king what you did to Jericho and its king. But this time you may keep its goods and animals for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city."
So Joshua and the whole army got ready to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand of his best fighting men and sent them out at night.
He ordered them, "Listen. Hide behind the city and wait. Do not go far from it. All of you stay ready.
I and all the people with me will come up to the city. When the men of Ai come out against us as they did before, we will run away from them.
They will chase us until we have drawn them away from the city, because they will say, 'They are running from us like last time.' While we run,
you get up from your hiding place and take the city. The LORD your God will give it into your hands.
When you have taken the city, set it on fire. Do what the LORD has said. These are my orders."
Then Joshua sent them off. They went to their hiding place and waited between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai. But Joshua spent that night with the people.
Early the next morning Joshua gathered the army, and he and the leaders of Israel led them up to Ai.
All the fighting men with him went up close to the city and camped north of Ai, with a valley between them and the city.
Joshua had taken about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
So the soldiers took their places: the main army north of the city and the ambush west of it. That night Joshua went down into the valley.
When the king of Ai saw this, he and all his men hurried out early in the morning to fight Israel at the place facing the Jordan valley. He did not know that men were hiding behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel pretended to be beaten, and they ran toward the desert.
All the men in Ai were called out to chase them. They chased Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
Not one man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city wide open while they chased Israel.
Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Hold out the spear in your hand toward Ai, because I will give the city to you." So Joshua held out his spear toward the city.
As soon as he did this, the men in hiding rose up quickly and ran into the city. They took it and quickly set it on fire.

The men of Ai looked back and saw smoke rising from the city into the sky. They had no chance to escape in any direction, because the Israelites who had been running toward the desert turned back against them.
When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city and smoke was rising from it, they turned around and attacked the men of Ai.
The men in the city also came out against them, so the men of Ai were trapped in the middle, with Israelites on both sides. Israel struck them down until none were left alive and none escaped.
But they captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

Israel finished killing all the men of Ai in the fields and the desert where they had chased them. When every one of them had fallen by the sword, all Israel went back to Ai and killed those who were in it.
Twelve thousand men and women died that day, all the people of Ai.
Joshua did not lower the hand holding out his spear until he had destroyed everyone who lived in Ai.
But Israel kept the animals and goods of the city for themselves, as the LORD had told Joshua.
So Joshua burned Ai and made it a ruin forever, an empty place still today.

He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening. At sunset Joshua ordered them to take the body down and throw it at the entrance of the city gate. They piled a large heap of stones over it, which is still there today.
Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites. It was written in the book of the law of Moses: an altar of uncut stones, which no iron tool had touched. On it they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to the LORD.
There, while the Israelites watched, Joshua wrote on the stones a copy of the law that Moses had written.

All Israel, foreigners and Israelites alike, with their leaders, officers and judges, stood on both sides of the covenant box of the LORD, facing the Levite priests who carried it. Half of them stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal. Moses, the servant of the LORD, had told them to do this when the people of Israel were first blessed.
Then Joshua read all the words of the law, the blessings and the curses, just as they are written in the book of the law.
He read every word Moses had commanded. He did not leave out one. He read it to the whole gathering of Israel, including the women, the children and the foreigners living among them.
